land.text: Erzincan with Kemah, Divriği and Şebinkarahisar: the four regions the page names

predecessors.note: The founder 'was probably one of the commanders of the Great Seljuk' and the principality 'seems to have been founded in the years following the battle' of Manzikert (Mengujekids page); the Erzincan page: 'In 1071 Erzincan was absorbed into the Mengüjek'.

successors.note: The Erzincan branch 'was subjugated by the Sultanate of Rum in 1228' (Mengujekids page).
'The Divriği branch was ended by the Ilkhanate in 1277' (Mengujekids page).

capitals.name: Erzincan
capitals.note: The page names no capitals, only the regions Erzincan, Kemah, Şebinkarahisar and Divriği; Erzincan is the seat of the senior branch after 1142 and the first place the Erzincan page ties to the Mengüjek (1071). Bridge at confidence 1.

capitals.name: Divriği
capitals.note: The Divriği branch is the surviving seat after 1228 (bridge at confidence 1).

correction.text: Erzincan with Kemah, Divriği and Şebinkarahisar: the four regions the page names

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Mengujekids). The page names Erzincan, Kemah, Şebinkarahisar and Divriği as the principality's regions without dates or an area. After İshak's death in 1142 'the beylik was split into the Erzincan and Divriği branches'; the split moves no border. Kemah is drawn inside Erzincan province; Divriği and Şebinkarahisar as 40 and 30 km discs.

New keyframe. 'The Erzincan branch was subjugated by the Sultanate of Rum in 1228'; the Divriği branch survives to 1277 as a Rum vassal (it recognized Rum on its copper coins) and was 'ended by the Ilkhanate in 1277'. Şebinkarahisar's fate is on no page and it is dropped with the Erzincan branch at confidence 1.

region.text: Erzincan with Kemah, Divriği and Şebinkarahisar: the four regions the page names

ledger.counterpart: holder not named by the page
ledger.note: 1072: Mengüjek Gazi founds the principality after Manzikert. The ruler list gives 'Mengüjek Gazi 1072-1118'; the principality 'seems to have been founded in the years following the battle'; the Erzincan page: 'In 1071 Erzincan was absorbed into the Mengüjek'. The pages name no previous holder.

1228: the Sultanate of Rum subjugates the Erzincan branch: 'The Erzincan branch was subjugated by the Sultanate of Rum in 1228.' The page does not name Kayqubad; the sultanate-of-rum dossier does not yet record it.
1228: Şebinkarahisar is closed with the Erzincan branch at confidence 1; no page opened says who held it or when it passed.
1277: the Ilkhanate ends the Divriği branch ('The Divriği branch was ended by the Ilkhanate in 1277'), the last Mengujekid holding.
1277: the Mengujekid dynasty ends with the Divriği branch.

wars.name: Rum subjugation of the Erzincan branch
wars.outcome: The Sultanate of Rum subjugated the Erzincan branch in 1228; the Erzincan page records the town's destruction in 1243 in fighting between Kaykhusraw II and the Mongols.

wars.name: Ilkhanid end of the Divriği branch
wars.outcome: The Ilkhanate ended the Divriği branch in 1277.

certainty.note: Four regions named without frontiers; discs round Divriği and Şebinkarahisar and the province of Erzincan are approximations.

sources.title: Erzincan
sources.note: 1071 absorption of Erzincan into the Mengüjek; 1243; nothing on 1228 or Kemah, Şebinkarahisar, Divriği.

sources.title: Divriği
sources.note: Opened for the Mengujekid history: the Great Mosque and hospital, no dates; nothing used for events.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Three pages opened; the Mengujekids page gives no area, capitals or acquisitions. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Rulers: Mengüjek Gazi 1072-1118, İshak 1118-1142; Erzincan branch Davudşah 1142-1162, Süleymanşah 1151-1162, Fahrettin Behramşah 1162-1225, Alaeddin Davudşah II 1225-1228; Divriği branch Süleyman 1142-1162, Şahinşah 1162-1198, Süleyman II 1198-1227, Ahmetşah 1227-1251, Melik Salih 1251-1277. The ruler strip is omitted because two branches run in parallel from 1142.
Not settled: acquisitions (none dated); whether Kemah and Şebinkarahisar belonged to which branch (Kemah is drawn inside Erzincan province, Şebinkarahisar dropped at 1228); the Erzincan page says the Mongols and Kaykhusraw II fought at Erzincan in 1243 (the sultanate-of-rum dossier has the Mongol capture of Erzincan in 1243). Vassalage to the Seljuks of Rum belongs to the sultanate-of-rum dossier: the earliest Şahinşah coin, dated 1171-2, bears Kilij Arslan II's name ('most likely ... servitude'), Behramşah was allied to Rum by marriage by 1178, and Divriği coins name Rum as overlord; none of these is dated as a vassal_start on the pages.
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Divriği, Şebinkarahisar.
